tr.td: Profiling
slow: the step takes longer than it should.
Step time or TFLOP/s first. Then, from a trace, how much of the step the all-to-all leaves exposed.
Interconnect
slow on several nodes: when NCCL falls back to TCP sockets, our EP16 proxy ran about 25 times slower, 1.7 against 42.0 TFLOP/s.

With NCCL_DEBUG=INFO, check "Using network" for the intended transport: IB for InfiniBand or Libfabric for the OFI plugin on EFA; Socket indicates fallback. Then compare nccl-tests alltoall bus bandwidth inside and across nodes (2.1), and TFLOP/s at node-local versus cross-node EP.
Overlap
slow: the all-to-all is not hidden behind compute.
Memory
OOM: one rank runs out of memory. slow: recomputation, or offload reloads that outlast compute, add step time.

Compare step time and peak memory after each change. Use the busiest rank's peak: maximum torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() across ranks or per-rank --record-memory-history snapshots. Longer backward can expose offload reloads that outlast compute.
Group-limited routing
slow: each token fans out across nodes.
How many nodes each token reaches (routing trace and the map of experts to ranks), and the tokens each EP rank receives (token counts), A.1.
Capacity and replicas
learns badly: tokens are dropped silently. OOM: one rank runs out of memory.
Share of dropped token-expert assignments per layer, 1 - kept / (tokens * topk), from a router forward hook, alongside validation loss. The routing trace skips records with drops.
Precision
slow: no speedup over bf16. learns badly: a higher loss than bf16.

Relative loss difference against a BF16 run of the same config across training; DeepSeek's 16B and 230B runs and Ling-1T stayed below 0.25%. Under NVFP4, also count exactly zero expert weight-gradient elements: these reached 7% of all parameters in Nemotron 3 Super.
